meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (unitary national jurisdiction; registered seat in Canton of Zug)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (germano-romanistic tradition with cantonal regulatory autonomy and federal direct-democratic overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 13 April 2010, replacing the 1986 BIT)
Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and Capital (DTA, in force 11 July 2014)
Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of Other States (ICSID, ratified by Switzerland 1968)
Switzerland–EU Free Trade Agreement (1972) and EU–Switzerland Bilateral Agreements I/II
EFTA Convention and Swiss Free Trade Agreements with emerging-market economies

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: SR 955.0 – Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG); SR 955.01 – Ordinance on the Prevention of Money Laundering; SR 311.0 – Swiss Criminal Code, Art. 305bis and 305ter; Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (Transparenzgesetz/UBO Register Act) of 16 June 2023, in force as at 1 November 2024; SR 221.411 – Ordinance on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV); SR 220 – Swiss Code of Obligations (OR); FINMA Circular 2018/5 on money-laundering due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of the ultimate beneficial owner(s), directors and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the UBO's country of origin (passport issuance authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization where the origin state is not a Hague Convention member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / current extract of foreign corporate shareholder or parent entity (if UBO is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating commercial register or company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of capital funds (pay-in verification for the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss licensed bank or financial intermediary receiving the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Swiss notarized attestation; no apostille required for use within Switzerland

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuten) and share subscription statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Swiss notarization; apostille required only if the instrument is presented before foreign authorities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth/source of funds declaration executed by the UBO (including COD e-commerce revenue origin)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public or licensed fiduciary in Zug
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature; apostille required when executed by a foreign notary in a Hague member state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, signatories, counters-parties and payment-rails partners (Airwallex, local logistics remittance agents) against: SECO/SNB/FINMA consolidated Swiss embargo and sanctions lists (SR 946.231), UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU restrictive measures, OFAC SDN list, PEP and adverse-media databases, and Interpol notices. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for PEPs, politically exposed persons from emerging markets, and persons connected to cash-intensive payment settlement. All screening results must be documented and retained in the AML/CFT file for at least five years post-termination of the business relationship under AMLA Art. 7.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex) maintained by the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IGE/IPI) – online at zefix.ch; filing and name examination conducted via the Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin/Roman characters; the working language of the Zug Commercial Register is German. Foreign trade names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; names must comply with the Swiss truthfulness, distinctiveness, and non-deception principles under Art. 33–35 HRegV. The legal form designation 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the suffix 'AG' is mandatory at the end of the name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File a written request for re-examination with the Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug within 30 days of the rejection decision, stating the reasons why the name satisfies Art. 33–35 HRegV. If rejected again, lodge an administrative appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority (Volkswirtschaftsdirektion des Kantons Zug) within 30 days under the Swiss Federal Act on Administrative Procedure (VwVG, SR 172.021). A further appeal lies to the Administrative Court of the Canton of Zug and ultimately to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht). An application for a preliminary name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible but restricted. A virtual/domiciliation office in Zug is acceptable for an e-commerce COD enterprise, provided that: (i) the domiciliation provider holds a cantonal licence for commercial domiciliation (gewerbsmässige Domizilhaltung); (ii) the company maintains effective management substance in Switzerland with accessible books and records; (iii) the board of directors satisfies the Swiss-residency majority under Art. 718 OR (at least one Swiss-resident board member for a single-member board, and a majority of Swiss residents for multi-member boards); and (iv) no artificial structuring for tax or sanction-evasion purposes is present. Regulatory acceptance is moderate; pure shell arrangements are rejected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 22 percent quantified first-year probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection or mandatory information request, elevated for entities using shared domiciliation addresses in Zug; mitigation measures include a physical working space at the registered address, retention of original corporate records in Switzerland, and continuous cooperation with the commercial register and tax authorities.

Apostille of foreign corporate, passport and UBO documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620-763 (Stock Company law, as revised effective 1 January 2023), together with Articles 626-631a OR on incorporation procedure, Article 640 OR on minimum capital, and the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of registered office; coordination via the Federal Commercial Register platform (Zefix/RegOf) operated by the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI) with final publication by the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC/SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially certified Deed of Incorporation containing the Articles of Association (Statuten) together with the registration application (Anmeldung) filing submitted to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of CHF 100,000; at least 20% (minimum CHF 20,000) must be fully paid up at incorporation. The paid-in funds must be placed in a blocked bank account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank and evidenced by an unconditional banker's confirmation; no state escrow account is required under Swiss law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] AG. The founding shareholders having subscribed the entire share capital pursuant to the Deed of Incorporation, the Board hereby resolves: (1) to accept the subscription and payment of CHF 100,000 share capital, CHF 20,000 being recorded as paid up; (2) to adopt the registered office at [address], Canton of Zug; (3) to appoint [Name] as Chairperson and [Name] as Board member; (4) to appoint [Name] as Managing Director with sole signature authority and [Name] as second signatory; (5) to instruct the filing of the Commercial Register application and the execution of all ancillary declarations; (6) to authorize the opening of the Sperrkonto and the engagement of the audit firm. Approved unanimously. Signed by the Board of Directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the intended canton of registered office via the federal Zefix portal (www.zefix.ch).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request with the proposed corporate name, business purpose, and intended canton. The register verifies that the name is not identical or misleadingly similar to existing entries and that it complies with the naming rules, including the mandatory company suffix 'AG' or 'SA'. The name may be reserved for up to 90 days; no payment is required at this stage beyond the final registration fee.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation form
Power of attorney or passport copy of the authorized applicant
Declaration of business purpose in German, French, or Italian
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for conflict or misleading character, file an alternative name immediately with a written explanatory note differentiating the business scope and corporate identification; priority of the original filing date is preserved on the alternative name only if refiled within the statutory grace period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public (Notar) authorized in the canton of registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association (Statuten) covering corporate name, registered office, statutory purpose, share capital, share types, record date, board structure, and auditor appointment. Convene all founding shareholders before the notary, who verifies identity, legal capacity, and the legality of the provisions. Upon unanimous adoption, the deed is executed and certified; the notary transmits the deed for subsequent register filing.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed draft
Articles of Association in an official Swiss language
Passports or ID cards of the founding shareholders
Share subscription statement signed by each founder
Proof of residential or commercial address of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a deficiency note, correct the flagged clauses (e.g., purpose wording, share classes, or capital statement) and re-execute the deed before the same notary. Formal defects do not nullify the incorporation if cured by a supplementary notarial instrument prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked capital account (Sperrkonto) and bank confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or PostFinance; banker's confirmation submitted to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocking account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company in formation at a licensed Swiss bank. Deposit at least CHF 20,000 (20% of the CHF 100,000 statutory minimum). Obtain an unconditional written banker's confirmation certifying the deposit, the account holder, and the free disposal rights of the company upon registration; the bank releases the funds only upon presentation of the Commercial Register certificate.
required_dossiers: Account opening application
Notarized Deed of Incorporation or extract
AML/KYC identification documentation of all beneficial owners
Power of attorney for the account signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional beneficial ownership documentation or refuses the certificate due to insufficient funds, supplement the KYC file and top up the deposit; the banker's confirmation is reissued within 24 hours of compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of the statutory auditor or opt-out declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; audit firm registered in the Swiss audit register (Zugelassene Revisionsexperten) or qualified to sign the opt-out declaration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Board appoints a licensed statutory auditor (Revisionsstelle) unless the company meets the small-company thresholds under Article 727a OR (fewer than 10 full-time employees and total assets below CHF 4.6 million) permitting a limited audit or opt-out. If the opt-out is taken, the Board files the signed declaration of renunciation with the Commercial Register; otherwise the appointed audit firm issues its written acceptance.
required_dossiers: Board resolution appointing the audit firm
Written acceptance of the audit firm
Opt-out declaration signed by the Board where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the opted-out auditor challenges the classification, recalculate FTE and balance-sheet totals on Swiss GAAP FER; adjust the declaration to a limited audit (prüferische Durchsicht) as required and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Cantonal Commercial Register and issuance of legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via the electronic filing portal of the canton; final entry published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC/SHAB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration application electronically signed by all authorized Board signatories. Attach the notarial deed, articles of association, banker's confirmation, list of directors with signature powers, declarations of acceptance, and auditor appointment documents. The register reviews legality and accuracy; upon admission, the company acquires legal personality as an Aktiengesellschaft and receives a registration certificate and Swiss UID number (automatically communicated to federal tax authorities).
required_dossiers: Completed Anmeldung registration form
Notarially certified Deed of Incorporation
Banker's confirmation of paid-up capital
Board resolution with countersignatures of directors
List of directors with signature authority and declarations of acceptance
Auditor appointment or opt-out declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the register issues a query (Vorprüfung), cure within the statutory deadline by submitting an amended deed or corrected filing; for missing electronic signatures, re-authenticate the application via the authorized signatory and resubmit without payment of an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal tax and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for VAT and tax purposes; Cantonal Tax Administration for direct taxes; Swiss Social Security Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) and SUVA for payroll.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon Commercial Register entry, the company automatically receives its UID business identification number. Immediately thereafter, register for VAT if annual worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 (mandatory VAT registration; voluntary registration allowed for COD retail operations). Register the company as an employer with the AHV compensation office and enroll the directors and staff for accident insurance (SUVA). Retail mail-order and COD settlement require no sectoral federal operating license.
required_dossiers: UID certificate from the Commercial Register
VAT registration form EN/DE applying for VAT number
Estimated turnover declaration and anticipated sales channels
AHV employer registration form with payroll declaration
SUVA accident insurance enrolment application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is challenged due to missing EORI or cross-border logistics determinations, submit a written clarification of the place of supply under the VAT Act Article 1; late registration surcharges are cured by prompt self-declaration to ESTV with a written mitigation request.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Office for Economic Affairs (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit, AWA) as the general oversight body; State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) as the federal reference — no sectoral licensing board applies to ISIC 4791 mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — mail-order retail and COD logistics distribution are non-concessioned activities under Swiss law; only a general commercial register entry and labor/administrative registrations apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and the cantonal office of environmental protection; the Municipal Waste and Clean Air Authorities as executing organs.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full Environmental Impact Assessment required. Warehousing, pick-pack logistics, and last-mile delivery operations of ISIC 4791 fall below the mandatory threshold of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung-Verordnung, UVPV). The company is nonetheless subject to a registration/notification duty for packaging volumes and COD-return waste streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater is generated; discharges must comply with the Federal Water Protection Act (Gewässerschutzgesetz, GSchG) municipal sewer standards and absence of hazardous effluents. VOC emissions from stored consumer goods must remain below 200 kg solvent per year under the Chemical Ordinance (Chemikalienverordnung); packaging materials must meet the Packaging Ordinance (Verpackungsverordnung) recycling obligations, and COD-return goods are classified as municipal commercial waste requiring separation and documented disposal under the Ordinance on Waste Movements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: mandatory inspection and fire-prevention clearance by the cantonal fire authority (Feuerpolizei/Kantonaler Gebäudeversicherung) covering premises, alarm systems, and emergency exits. Structural load inspection: verification certificate from the cantonal building inspectorate confirming that the warehouse and office floors meet the load-bearing standards for storage racking and parcel sortation equipment. Workplace clearance: health-and-safety verification by SUVA and the cantonal labor inspectorate for office, picking, and delivery staff, including first-aid provision, accident-prevention training, and ergonomic assessments.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/SFTA) – Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer (Main VAT Division), via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration portal (www.estv.admin.ch) and the Swiss Business Register (Zefix/RegOf/UID Register) operated by the Federal Statistical Office and the Federal Commercial Register Office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that is not resident in Switzerland but carries out taxable activities in Switzerland must register for Swiss VAT/UIDS after exceeding CHF 100,000 worldwide turnover from taxable activities, unless exempt. The foreign entity must appoint a Swiss-based tax representative to register with the SFTA, obtain a Swiss business identification number (UID) from the Federal Commercial Register, and file a registration form via the Swiss GST portal. For income tax purposes, a Swiss AG is registered with the cantonal tax authority of its seat and receives a cantonal tax number; non-resident shareholders would not need a Swiss TIN solely for shareholding. The statutory VAT and UID procedures are administered through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration and the Federal Commercial Register Office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections similar to the United States. A Swiss AG is mandatorily taxed at entity level at the federal, cantonal, and communal levels. The group consolidation option under Swiss corporate tax law (Steuerkonsolidierung) permits profit-transfer agreements among group companies, but this is an intercorporate consolidation mechanism rather than an entity classification election. For VAT, an election to tax real estate and to waive VAT exemption is available for immovable property transactions under Art. 22 Swiss VAT Act; foreign parent entities may use hybrid mismatch rules under OECD/G20 BEPS recommendations, but they must be aligned with domestic anti-abuse provisions implemented in Swiss tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of worldwide taxable turnover from supplies of goods and services, excluding capital investment income, unless the entity is a foreign business making exclusively VAT-exempt supplies in Switzerland, in which case no registration is due; special thresholds apply to radio and television broadcasting services and to distance selling.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate a real-time fiscal clearance, fiscal API, or digital stamping regime for ordinary B2B or B2C VAT invoices. Swiss VAT invoices must contain mandatory data: supplier name and address, UID number, buyer name and address, date of supply, nature and quantity of the goods/services, consideration, and the applicable VAT rate. E-invoicing using Swiss QR-bills or the Swiss payment standards is recognised. No government pre-clearance or real-time validation API is imposed; however, all invoices and accounting records must be retained and be accessible to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration upon audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported by a Swiss supplier to a foreign consignee or to a foreign country are zero-rated for Swiss VAT (Art. 23 VAT Act), provided the export is evidenced and the goods physically leave Switzerland. Services related to movable tangible property, services relating to immovable property, and other B2B services supplied to foreigners are zero-rated where they are used abroad and meet conditions in Art. 8 VAT Act. The supplier must be able to demonstrate with supporting documentation that the export occurred and that the recipient is established abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration via Swiss Customs e-dec)
Bill of Lading or airway bill as transport evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of payment from abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating or submission of false documentary evidence constitutes tax evasion under the Swiss federal tax law, leading to fines equal to the tax evaded (plus penalty), interest, claim enhancement, and potential criminal imprisonment for wilful fraud. The SFTA may retroactively adjust VAT assessments within the limitation period of 10 years for intentional tax evasion, and 5 years for gross negligence, and will claw back any erroneously zero-rated VAT plus statutory interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank, Bundesplatz 1, Bern), which conducts monetary policy and operates the SIC payment and settlement system; prudential supervision of banks and financial intermediaries is exercised by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA, Laupenstrasse 27, Bern).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Swiss law imposes no general exchange-control restrictions on capital inflows, profit remittance, dividend distributions, liquidation proceeds, or external financing. Prior approval by the SNB or FINMA is not required for transfers to or from non-resident accounts, and counterparty emerging-market capital controls are the only practical friction. Residual legal constraints arise solely from binding international sanctions implemented by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and from FINMA's withholding-tax and operational rules. For a Cash-on-Delivery e-commerce model, collection proceeds may be accumulated offshore and repatriated in freely usable currency at any time, provided each flow is reconciled with the underlying commercial transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland has no statutory export-proceeds surrender regime. Exporters are not required to repatriate foreign-currency earnings within a fixed period, convert them into CHF, or hold them in Switzerland. Receipts may be maintained in FX accounts with Swiss or foreign banks. Nevertheless, under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) and FINMA Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA), banks must identify the economic background of any cash-related or unusual flows; cash-equivalent COD collections passing through third-party logistics agents must be contractually attributable to the Swiss AG, and transactions of CHF 15,000 or more in cash or near-cash must be treated as client-identification triggers.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for the AG incorporation deposit and multi-currency Operational Account (CHF, EUR, USD) with SIC, SEPA, and SWIFT access
Capital Escrow Account under Art. 632-633 CO and Operational Account with e-commerce payment integration and trade finance desk
Operational Account; escrow confirmation possible through affiliated cantonal Raiffeisen bank for locally incorporated AG with Swiss nexus
Operational Account with strong collection-rail and logistics-payment integrations; escrow functionality limited

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Cantonale Vaudoise (BCV), Place St-Francois 14, Lausanne
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for non-resident-owned AGs; product fit for francophone emerging-market corridors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as a secondary treasury execution rail; Low as a substitute for the statutory banking relationship. Airwallex is a globally licensed payments platform (e.g., UK FCA EMI authorisation and other EEA/common-law licences) rather than a FINMA-authorised Swiss bank. The AG may open an Airwallex account for low-value cross-border disbursements to logistics partners and supplier payouts, but: (i) the statutory share-capital escrow deposit must be held with a Swiss bank authorised by FINMA and evidenced by the Art. 633 CO Bankbestaetigung; (ii) Airwallex cannot issue the notarial confirmation required for commercial-register filing; (iii) primary correspondent liquidity should remain with a Tier-1 Swiss bank; and (iv) all AMLA documentation - UBO declarations, source-of-wealth evidence, and transaction monitoring - must still be supported by the Swiss ring-fenced banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Medium-Risk Enhanced corporate client in cash-intensive e-commerce, remote onboarding is generally insufficient. Most Tier-1 Swiss banks require an in-person KYC interview with at least one authorised director or a Swiss officer holding signatory power, conducted at the branch or before a Swiss notary or consular officer with legalised ID and original commercial-register extract. A Swiss registered agent (formation office) with a board power of attorney can partially substitute, but the beneficial owners must still be identified. If any UBO resides in a high-risk or sanctions-adjacent jurisdiction, face-to-face verification or embassy-legalised documentation will be mandatory, and FINMA Circular 2016/07 video-identification applies only to low-risk retail clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-on-Delivery model generating high-volumes of small cash-equivalent receipts in emerging markets via local logistics intermediaries, without a clear custody and reconciliation chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed logistics and COD collection agreements with each courier; detailed cash-handling protocol (daily collection, segregation, courier-to-bank deposit, aggregated remittance schedule); order-to-cash reconciliation reports; excerpts of the order management and logistics systems showing the payment chain; AML/CFT risk assessment of the collection jurisdictions; and board-approved transaction thresholds and monitoring rules for the logistics provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership structure with UBOs located in jurisdictions with weak beneficial-ownership transparency, or PEP exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart and constitutive documents evidencing Swiss substance; UBO declaration forms with embassy or notarially certified identity documents; business plan, cash-flow forecast, and commercial contracts validating the emerging-market COD corridor; Swiss tax residence certificates; and written confirmation that no foreign-currency surrender or capital-control obligations conflict with the Swiss AG's treasury operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared corporate purpose (mail-order retail) and early capital flows, or funding via shareholder loans and third-party advances before revenue materialises
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising funding; written shareholder loan agreements at arm's-length terms with repayment schedule; source-of-funds evidence from the lending party; pro-forma invoice register and logistics contracts modelling the volume ramp-up; appointment of a Swiss statutory auditor under the audit requirement rules if requested by the bank; and periodic management accounts reconciling deployed capital to inventory and marketing spend.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The registered minimum capital for the AG is CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 50,000 must be paid in before registration. Routing: (i) the shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA CT to the blocked Capital Escrow Account under the name 'CH_AG in Gruendung' (or 'CH_AG SA en formation') at the Swiss bank; (ii) remittance information (Field 70) should state 'KAPITALEINLAGE / APPORTS EN ESPECES' together with the prospective CHE commercial-register number and share-class reference; (iii) the bank issues the Art. 633 CO Bankbestaetigung confirming the funds are at the board's free disposal; (iv) the notary certifies the deed and files the registration; (v) subsequent working-capital injections and shareholder loans should be labelled as 'DARLEHEN VON AKTIONAER' or 'PRET D'ACTIONNAIRE' under documented loan agreements to prevent recharacterisation as hidden dividend reserves subject to Swiss 35% withholding tax; (vi) all flows are captured by the bank's reporting for SNB balance-of-payments statistics.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for standard single supplier and logistics payments, with Field 70 carrying the invoice and contract references and pre-screening against SECO and international sanctions lists; (ii) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit under ICC UCP 600 for high-value inventory procurement, issued in CHF, USD, or EUR through the Swiss bank's correspondent network; (iii) domestic CHF settlement via SIC, euro settlement via SEPA, and USD via the bank's New York correspondent account; (iv) batch aggregated remittances from the COD logistics collection partner to the AG's operational account, followed by reinvestment into supplier MT103s; (v) multi-currency sweeps to Airwallex for last-mile payouts to local logistics and collection agents in the target emerging markets; and (vi) full audit trail retained for the statutory audit file and for FINMA record-keeping obligations under AMLA Article 7.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright OTC FX forwards in major pairs (CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, USD/EUR) with tenors of up to 12-24 months, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or the Swiss Master Agreement for OTC Derivatives

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing the emerging-market currencies of the COD target jurisdictions, allowing hedge of receivables without onshore physical settlement, executed exclusively with FINMA-authorised Swiss banks or their branches
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps) to convert CHF shareholder-loan funding into USD- or EUR-denominated working capital matched to trade receivable maturities
Short-dated FX swaps for liquidity management of timing mismatches between COD cash collections and supplier payment dates

Exchange-traded currency futures and listed FX options on Eurex, or OTC options with Swiss banking counterparties, subject to board authorization and the internal risk-management duties of Art. 717 of the Swiss Code of Obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, annual report and proposal for appropriation of profit (AGM approval under Art. 698-699 OR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None filed; presented to the ordinary shareholders' meeting and retained in company records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance-sheet date; a calendar-year AG must be held by 30 June unless a court-approved extension is obtained
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors remain liable for damages; dividends cannot be validly resolved; shareholders may petition the court to order convening of the general meeting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, including federal/cantonal/communal tax self-assessment and capital tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Direct Federal Tax is also administered by cantonal authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No uniform federal deadline; cantonal statutes govern, commonly 30 April-30 June after the calendar year end, with extension on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on underpaid tax, late filing penalties, estimated tax assessment if no return is filed, and execution proceedings for unpaid amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return and annual VAT settlement (if the AG is liable for Swiss VAT on mail-order/COD sales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each VAT reporting period; frequency assigned by ESTV (annual, semi-annual or quarterly)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, late filing fines under Art. 102 VAT Act, and administrative penalties up to CHF 10,000 for intentional non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial register event-driven notifications (Switzerland does not impose an annual return or annual commercial-register renewal filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual deadline; each factual change in registered seat, board, capital, articles or representation must be filed after the change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court imposing fines for late registration; ex officio dissolution if the company no longer has a valid registered office or required corporate organ

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit report (ordinary audit, limited audit or valid opt-out) and auditor's report to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None filed; report must be made available to shareholders and kept with the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before or at the ordinary shareholders' meeting, within 6 months after the balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: General meeting cannot validly approve the annual accounts without the required audit report; director and auditor liability under Art. 755/759 OR

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit is mandatory if the company exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, annual average 250 full-time employees. A limited audit applies below these thresholds unless validly waived; audit must also be conducted if a shareholder holding 10% of the share capital requires it, if the company is listed, or if it has issued bonds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963b OR); Swiss GAAP FER is accepted for presentation; IFRS is required for listed issuers and accepted for AGs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not currently require an annual UBO confirmation filing to a central register. Each share transfer requires the board to update the shareholders' register; bearer-share beneficial-owner declarations and AML client-file UBO data are updated on actual knowledge of ownership changes. Annual voluntary reconciliation at the balance-sheet date is standard practice for the AG.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share ledger under Art. 686 OR)
Register of Directors and Auditors (board election records)
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Meetings
Annual accounts, audit reports and supporting books (retained for 10 years)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 900-3,500 (approx. USD 1,000-4,000) per year for registered office, mail handling and local representation services; additional fees apply if a resident-director service is required
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Limited audit CHF 3,000-8,000 (approx. USD 3,500-9,400); ordinary audit CHF 15,000-50,000 (approx. USD 17,000-59,000) depending on turnover, transactions and group complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Swiss federal direct tax is 8.5% on corporate profit after tax, equal to 7.83% on a pre-tax basis. Cantons and municipalities levy separate corporate income taxes in a range of approximately 4.2% to 14.5%, producing aggregate combined headline rates from about 11.9% to 21.6% depending on the canton of residence.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general Swiss federal tax holiday exists. Cantons may grant temporary tax relief of 40% to 50% for up to 10 years for newly established Swiss AGs that create jobs and have genuine economic substance. At federal level, a 95% participation exemption under Art. 69 DBG applies to qualifying dividends and capital gains; several cantons provide research and development super-deductions. The effective aggregate rate for an active e-commerce trading company is usually between 14% and 21% before cantonal capital tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss combined federal/cantonal corporate tax return for legal entities; the AG files via the cantonal tax authority's official electronic portal using ESTV-certified tax software for the federal direct tax part.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return is due within six months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year AG the cantonal deadline is commonly 30 June of the following year, with extensions available where complete financial statements have been prepared and professional representation is used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification of the AG: company name, legal form, commercial register UID number, registered office in Switzerland, board members and authorised signatories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must identify a Swiss registered office and an address available for service. A non-resident-owned AG must still appoint a director or representative resident or sufficiently connected to Switzerland; a foreign-only mailbox management is an audit red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and operating revenue from mail-order retail, ISIC 4791, including cash-on-delivery collections remitted by logistics partners and payment service providers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue is taxable in the AG even if sales originate from an emerging-market logistics hub; deferred cash receipts and COD cash floats must be included in the Swiss balance sheet and not treated as shareholder loans.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, freight, customs, warehouse and logistics distribution expenses; deduction of payment processing fees, chargebacks, refunds and COD collection fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to related non-resident logistics companies must comply with transfer pricing documentation and be supported by invoices; absence of Arm's Length evidence leads to recharacterisation as a hidden dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Personnel expenses, employer pension contributions, Swiss social security contributions and any payroll obligations arisen from employees in Switzerland.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors' fees may be deductible only if real services are performed and registered; excessive management fees paid to foreign holding or sister entities are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation and amortisation of fixed assets, IT systems, warehouse equipment and intangibles used in the COD e-commerce operation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Depreciation rates must follow cantonal practice; depreciation of a non-Swiss brand transferred into the AG must be based on an actual arm's-length acquisition and can trigger Swiss withholding tax if not properly structured.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit before loss carryforward and participation relief; this line reconciles commercial accounting profit to Swiss fiscal standards including non-deductible expenses and tax-free income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All income and expense allocable to Swiss permanent establishment must be reported in the Swiss AG; no foreign income exclusion or remittances-exempt regime applies unless a valid tax treaty declares the AG fiscally resident outside Switzerland, which is rare.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward deduction from prior tax years, limited to seven consecutive years under Swiss federal and cantonal practice.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A change of shareholders or relocation of the emerging-market COD business does not automatically cancel carried losses if the business substance continues, but an abuse restructuring may be denied under Art. 210 DBG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of federal direct tax at 8.5% on taxable profit after tax; the same return reports the cantonal and municipal tax base using the applicable statutory rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG is the taxpayer; non-resident shareholders have no direct filing obligation for the AG's income. Dividend distributions and any hidden distributions are separately subject to Swiss anticipatory tax of 35%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing after a reminder triggers a disciplinary fine of up to CHF 10,000, default interest of approximately 5% per annum, and the possible issue of an estimated assessment shifting the burden of proof to the AG. Intentional false declaration or suppression of COD revenue is treated as tax evasion and can produce a fine of up to 100% of the evaded tax, with criminal proceedings against responsible directors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Swiss withholding tax return on anticipatory tax, filed electronically with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration under the Federal Act on Withholding Tax (Verrechnungssteuergesetz).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after the end of each calendar quarter; ordinary commercial interest and royalties outside taxable instruments do not require a quarterly return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross distributions by the AG: cash dividends, constructive dividends, hidden profit transfers, in-kind distributions and benefits granted to shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG must deduct Swiss anticipatory tax of 35% from the gross distribution and remit it to ESTV. Failure to withhold creates direct personal liability of the board of directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest and other proceeds subject to withholding tax, including interest on bonds, money-market instruments and bank deposits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on ordinary commercial trade loans, factoring lines and logistics settlement accounts is not subject to Swiss withholding tax unless issued in tradable securities form; non-resident lenders should document the debt instrument carefully to avoid reclassification as equity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of anticipatory tax withheld, date of payment and confirmation of remittance to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders in treaty countries may claim partial refund by submitting a valid Tax Residency Certificate and a refund application to ESTV within three years after the calendar year of distribution; without a DTA the 35% withholding is final.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-remittance of Swiss anticipatory tax carries default interest, an administrative fine of up to 100% of the withheld amount in wilful cases, and personal liability of directors because the withheld tax is trust property of the state.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer / impot anticipe) on all dividend and constructive distributions made by the Swiss AG.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss AG first withholds 35% at source. The non-resident shareholder then applies to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration for a refund of the difference between 35% and the residual treaty rate. The protocol is: (1) obtain the Tax Residency Certificate from the shareholder's jurisdiction covering the dividend payment period; (2) obtain confirmation from the Swiss paying bank or custodian of the gross dividend and Swiss tax withheld; (3) file the official ESTV refund request with the Tax Residency Certificate and supporting custody statements; (4) submit the application within three years after the end of the calendar year in which the distribution was made. No treaty relief is available without an applicable DTA; an emerging-market shareholder without a Swiss treaty generally receives no refund and the 35% withholding is final.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law does not impose withholding tax on royalties, licence fees or technical service fees paid by a Swiss AG to a foreign recipient. Ordinary interest on commercial loans is also outside Swiss anticipatory tax unless the debt is documented as a bond, money-market paper or Swiss bank deposit. Under Swiss tax treaties, interest and royalty residual rates are usually 0% to 10%, but because Switzerland does not impose domestic source tax on such payments, no domestic withholding is collected; the key Swiss risk is recharacterisation of excessive royalties or interest as hidden dividend distributions, which then become subject to 35% anticipatory tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 10,000,000 in aggregate gross related-party transactions in a tax year is the practical Swiss threshold that triggers the expectation of contemporaneous OECD transfer pricing documentation, including a Local File and, where applicable, a Master File. Below this threshold, the Swiss tax authority may still request a benchmarking study, functional analysis or TP policy when cross-border flow from emerging-market logistics or COD settlement creates audit risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the Swiss GAAR under Art. 210 DBG and OECD treaty anti-avoidance rules require genuine economic substance. A Swiss AG in mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery must maintain real premises, employees, board meetings, decision-making functions, bank accounts and cash flow control in Switzerland. The foreign emerging-market logistics hub must be a distinct and substantiated function, not an artificial arrangement to shift profit; otherwise the Swiss authorities may recharacterise the structure, deny treaty relief and impose 35% Swiss withholding tax on constructive distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of cash-on-delivery revenue, diversion of logistics remittances to private accounts, off-book cash management, understated inventory, or falsification of records showing COD settlements as shareholder loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of federal and cantonal taxes, penalty interest of about 5% per annum, and administrative penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax; qualified tax fraud with falsified documents may impose criminal penalties including imprisonment for responsible persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under Swiss corporate law for damages caused by wilful or negligent management; in tax penal proceedings the responsible officer can be individually fined, and where hidden profits are distributed to non-resident shareholders the director may be liable for the AG's unpaid tax and withholding tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Keeping only a registered office in a low-tax Swiss canton, no Swiss employees, no operational oversight, board decisions taken abroad, cash management directed entirely from the emerging-market hub, and using the Swiss AG only to benefit from treaty protection or credibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of Swiss anti-abuse law under Art. 210 DBG, reallocation of income to the actual controlling owner, denial of DTA benefits, potential liquidation proceedings under commercial registry law, and penalty assessments for wilful failure to report substance changes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to restore withdrawn capital, are jointly liable for the company's tax debts in formal liquidation, and can face travel restrictions or entry bans through Swiss debt enforcement if unpaid tax liability is linked to concealment of assets abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive logistics fees to a related emerging-market company, granting the foreign parent an unreasonably high gross margin, or transferring COD cash float to shareholders without arm's-length interest; absence of a written TP policy and functional analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss tax authority makes an arm's-length adjustment and recharacterises the excess as a hidden profit distribution; the excess is subject to Swiss 35% withholding tax and can also be taxed as a non-deductible expense, plus late payment interest and penalties of up to 100% of the additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the non-arm's-length arrangement are jointly and severally liable for the withheld tax that should have been collected, and may face civil restitution for breach of fiduciary duties and criminal charges for disloyalty to the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring cash-on-delivery collection amounts to stay below reporting thresholds, commingling merchant receipts with shareholder money in Airwallex or local logistics wallets, and failing to maintain an audit trail of the CoD remittance chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss AML Act duties apply to financial intermediaries; implicated logistics or payment providers that intentionally circumvent KYC/STR obligations face criminal fines and imprisonment. The proceeds from structured or concealed CoD money flows may be confiscated under the Swiss Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly use unlicensed payment rails or direct the splitting of cash flows to conceal taxable revenue are individually exposed to criminal conviction, confiscation, civil damages, and asset-freezing or travel bans during criminal investigation.
